// File: lib/structure/exchangeContextCore/client/ensureSyncToken.ts
//
// Phase 3 (2026-09-04, first real implementation piece — design captured
// 2026-09-03, see docs/design/extensionPlan.txt section 7's "Live
// cross-tab/cross-process sync auth" section for the full reasoning this
// implements). The auth-friction problem: calling signInForSync on every
// single sync write would mean a signature/password prompt on every
// account switch — this caches the resulting bearer token client-side and
// refreshes it proactively, ahead of its own expiry, so a real write only
// ever pays the sign-in cost once per ~10 minutes, not once per write.
//
// Deliberately reuses getConnectedSigner() as the approval gate — the
// SAME chokepoint every other Merit-authorized write already passes
// through (see that file's own doc comment). No new security decision:
// minting a sync token is just "another Merit-gated write" as far as the
// approval/password-mode matrix is concerned.
//
// Token expiry is read directly out of the token itself (the
// `v1.<exp36>.<addressHex>.<sig>` format lib/server/spCoinAuth.ts's
// buildSessionToken produces) rather than assuming a client-side copy of
// the server's SESSION_TTL_MS constant — avoids the two ever silently
// drifting apart if that constant changes server-side.
//
// Proactive refresh, not reactive-401-retry (design decision already
// made, not re-litigated here): a timer re-mints the token
// REFRESH_LEAD_MS before it actually expires, so an in-flight write never
// races a token that's about to die mid-request. The refresh is
// deliberately fail-soft — if it can't get a signer right now (wallet
// locked, user navigated away, approval rejected), it just clears the
// cache silently and lets the next real ensureSyncToken() call retry
// through the normal path, which is already gated exactly the way any
// other real write is. A background timer must never surface an alarming
// error for something the user didn't directly ask for.
'use client';

import { getConnectedSigner } from '@/lib/spCoin/getConnectedSigner';
import { isSyncAuthorizationRequired, isSyncDisabled } from '@/components/wallet/lib/meritConnect';
import { signInForSync } from './exchangeContextClient';

/** How long before actual expiry to proactively re-mint — matches the design doc's "~8-9 minutes" against a 10-minute token (10min - 90s = 8.5min). */
const REFRESH_LEAD_MS = 90_000;

interface CachedToken {
  address: string;
  token: string;
  expiresAt: number;
}

let cached: CachedToken | null = null;
let refreshTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
let inFlight: { address: string; promise: Promise<string> } | null = null;

function clearScheduledRefresh() {
  if (refreshTimer !== null) {
    clearTimeout(refreshTimer);
    refreshTimer = null;
  }
}

/** Parses the expiry embedded in a token minted by lib/server/spCoinAuth.ts's buildSessionToken — returns null if the shape doesn't match (fails safe: caller treats it as already-expired rather than trusting an unparseable token's freshness). */
function parseTokenExpiresAt(token: string): number | null {
  const parts = token.split('.');
  if (parts.length !== 4) return null;
  const expiresAt = Number.parseInt(parts[1], 36);
  return Number.isFinite(expiresAt) && expiresAt > 0 ? expiresAt : null;
}

export interface EnsureSyncTokenParams {
  chainId: number;
  activeAccountAddress: string;
  rpcUrl: string;
  /** 2026-10-11: a person clicked something that needs this token (saving the active spCoin): the mint may show its own password / approval screen instead of failing silently, and it is not a background request. */
  userInitiated?: boolean;
}

async function mintToken(params: EnsureSyncTokenParams): Promise<CachedToken> {
  // Read once, used for both flags below — they're deliberately the same
  // question: "Sync Authorization Required" is the one thing that opts this
  // background mint INTO forcing its own password prompt. Off (the
  // default) means the opposite, not just "don't force" — this mint must
  // never pop its own interactive UI at all (2026-09-07, on request: "if
  // sync is turned off then we should use the stored password"). It should
  // silently ride on whatever password is already cached from a real user
  // action elsewhere (securityApproved() inside getConnectedSigner still
  // checks that first, unaffected by this flag) and fail soft — same as any
  // other background sync failure — when nothing is cached yet, rather than
  // forcing the Merit Wallet open and demanding one of its own. That's what
  // was actually happening before this fix: a cold-boot background push
  // popped "Authorize Sync" directly on top of the real "Unlock Merit
  // Wallet" sign-on screen, before the user had unlocked anything.
  const syncAuthRequired = isSyncAuthorizationRequired();
  const signer = await getConnectedSigner({
    chainId: params.chainId,
    activeAccountAddress: params.activeAccountAddress,
    rpcUrl: params.rpcUrl,
    label: 'Sync authorization',
    title: 'Authorize Sync',
    // This mints a token, it doesn't move funds or change on-chain state —
    // same category of low-stakes signature as any other read/auth flow
    // already in this app (see useCreateAccountForm.ts's identical
    // nonce/verify usage), not a transaction needing its own confirm UI.
    // Deliberately exempt from "All Transaction Approval Required" (see
    // that param's own doc comment) — this mint still gets its OWN,
    // independent password requirement right below, via the "Sync
    // Authorization Required" checkbox.
    skipMandatoryApprovalGate: true,
    forceRequirePassword: syncAuthRequired,
    interactive: syncAuthRequired || params.userInitiated === true,
    // 2026-09-07, found live: a real Uniswap swap retry hit "Another Merit
    // Wallet approval is already pending" because this exact background
    // mint had grabbed the shared approval slot moments earlier. See
    // approval.ts's MeritApprovalRequest.background doc comment — this is
    // the one real background caller of getConnectedSigner, so it's the
    // one place this flag is ever set true.
    background: params.userInitiated !== true,
  });
  const token = await signInForSync(params.activeAccountAddress, (message) => signer.signMessage(message));
  const expiresAt = parseTokenExpiresAt(token);
  if (expiresAt === null) {
    // Server returned a token this client can't parse the expiry from —
    // fail loudly here rather than caching something we can't safely
    // schedule a refresh for.
    throw new Error('ensureSyncToken: minted token has an unrecognized shape');
  }
  return { address: params.activeAccountAddress.toLowerCase(), token, expiresAt };
}

function scheduleRefresh(params: EnsureSyncTokenParams, expiresAt: number) {
  clearScheduledRefresh();
  const delay = Math.max(0, expiresAt - Date.now() - REFRESH_LEAD_MS);
  refreshTimer = setTimeout(() => {
    mintToken(params)
      .then((next) => {
        cached = next;
        scheduleRefresh(params, next.expiresAt);
      })
      .catch(() => {
        // Fail-soft — see this file's own header comment. Clear the stale
        // entry so the next real ensureSyncToken() call mints fresh
        // rather than serving a token that's about to expire.
        cached = null;
      });
  }, delay);
}

/**
 * Returns a bearer token valid for pushExchangeContextPatch, minting (and
 * gating through the normal Merit-approval chokepoint) only when there
 * isn't already a fresh one cached for this exact address.
 */
export async function ensureSyncToken(params: EnsureSyncTokenParams): Promise<string> {
  // "Application Synchronization" set to Disable (2026-09-07, see
  // MeritWalletConfig.syncMode's own doc comment) — the single outbound
  // chokepoint every sync pusher (the three
  // useCrossProcess*Sync hooks, walletState.tsx's own account/network sync,
  // tradeExecutionLockClient.ts) mints through before pushing anything.
  // Checked ahead of the cache hit on purpose: a token minted before the
  // checkbox was flipped must not keep letting pushes through afterward.
  // Clears any already-scheduled proactive refresh too, so nothing keeps
  // quietly re-minting in the background once this is on. Every caller is
  // already fail-soft on a thrown/rejected ensureSyncToken (this looks
  // identical to "the mint failed"), so no new error path for any of them.
  if (isSyncDisabled()) {
    clearScheduledRefresh();
    cached = null;
    throw new Error('ensureSyncToken: sync is disabled (Disable Sync checkbox, Config tab).');
  }
  const normalized = params.activeAccountAddress.toLowerCase();
  const now = Date.now();
  if (cached?.address === normalized && cached.expiresAt - now > REFRESH_LEAD_MS) {
    return cached.token;
  }
  // 2026-10-12: ONE mint at a time per account. Several callers asking at once (the account / network / token syncs all start when an account becomes active) used to each start their own mint, and with MetaMask each mint is a
  // signature request: the person saw the same "Account Write Authorization" prompt three or four times. Callers that arrive while a mint is running now share its result.
  if (inFlight?.address === normalized) return inFlight.promise;
  const promise = mintToken(params)
    .then((minted) => {
      cached = minted;
      scheduleRefresh(params, minted.expiresAt);
      return minted.token;
    })
    .finally(() => {
      if (inFlight?.promise === promise) inFlight = null;
    });
  inFlight = { address: normalized, promise };
  return promise;
}

/** Test-only escape hatch — clears the cache and any pending refresh timer so a fresh mint is forced next call. Not used by real app code. */
export function _resetSyncTokenCacheForTests() {
  cached = null;
  inFlight = null;
  clearScheduledRefresh();
}
